transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess the biggest reason I finally made the appointment is my sleep. It’s gotten really unreliable, and I feel like it’s starting to run my life a little bit. I’ll be exhausted by the end of the day—like, I’ll get into bed thinking I should be asleep in five minutes—but then my brain just starts going.

I lie there replaying sales forecasts, things with my team, conversations I had during the day, things I might have missed, what could go wrong tomorrow… and it’s not even productive, it’s just like this loop I can’t shut off. Then if I do fall asleep, I’ve been waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and once I’m up, that’s it. My mind turns back on immediately, and I can’t get it to power down again.

So, yeah… I’m here because I’m tired, but not just normal tired. It’s more like I can’t trust that I’ll actually sleep, even when I really need to.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even when things are going okay?

I don’t know that I’d say depressed, exactly. I mean, I get frustrated and worn down, but it feels more tied to not sleeping and feeling like I’m constantly trying to keep up. I haven’t really noticed that I’ve lost interest in things in a big way… like if I actually have time and energy, I still want to do the things I normally enjoy.

It’s more that I don’t always get to enjoy them because I’m tired or distracted. But emotionally, I wouldn’t describe it as being down all the time, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things, even when there’s not much you can do about them, and does it feel hard to control those worries?

Yes. Definitely. That’s probably the part that feels the most… I don’t know, embarrassing? Because I can be very logical about it at first. Like I’ll literally tell myself, “Brenda, you’ve done the plan, you’ve made the list, you’ve sent the email, there’s nothing else to do right now—let it go.” And for maybe five minutes I can convince myself I’m being reasonable.

But then something else pops up. I’ll think, okay, what if that forecast is too optimistic, or what if I missed some detail in a conversation, or what if someone on my team is struggling and I didn’t catch it early enough. And even if I check one concern off, it’s like three more come in right behind it. It doesn’t feel like I’m choosing to think about it. It feels like my brain keeps opening new tabs and I can’t close them fast enough.

And I know that some of these things aren’t things I can solve at 11 at night or in the middle of the day when I’m supposed to be focusing on something else. I know that. But knowing it doesn’t really stop it. That’s the frustrating part.
